question.text: How does 'synchronized trading' differ from normal market trading?

answer.text: Synchronized trading involves coordinated buy and sell orders by connected parties placed within close time intervals to manipulate price or create false volume, whereas normal trading involves independent, uncoordinated market decisions
Synchronized trading occurs on multiple exchanges while normal trading occurs on a single exchange
There is no difference; synchronized trading is a legitimate trading strategy
Synchronized trading is always done through algorithmic trading while normal trading is manual

explanation.text: The Logic: Per workbook pages 153-154, the Sunita Gupta/Vishvas group case shows that synchronized trading involves connected parties placing buy and sell orders in close proximity of time, with repeated trades and a prior meeting of minds, used to manipulate LTP. Page 154 links synchronization and circularity to close time proximity and prior coordination, in contrast to independent, uncoordinated normal trading. The Trap: Option B describes cross-exchange trading or arbitrage rather than synchronized manipulation. Option D wrongly equates synchronized trading with algorithmic trading; algorithmic execution is a separate concept and not what defines the manipulation in this case. Note: The defining features from the source are coordinated counterparties, close time proximity, and an inferred prior meeting of minds.
